title: [Bug] Kimi-K3: `nvidia_kda` prefill produces NaN after ~1,800 tokens (Triton is correct)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. (Closest: #39971 and #41572, which are different code paths.)
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version. (Reproduced on v0.5.21; the vendored `kda_nvidia_prefill` package is unchanged on main at 2c2986b.)
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

With `--linear-attn-prefill-backend nvidia_kda`, Kimi-K3 prefill returns NaN once a sequence passes about 1,800 tokens. In the failing call, one KDA head (beta 0.93 to 1.0) drifts from about token 78 and grows roughly tenfold every 35 to 55 tokens until it overflows. The NaN is written to the KV cache and the recurrent state, so answers come back as `!!!!` with NaN logprobs, and later requests that reuse the prefix inherit it.

In serving, `NvidiaKDAKernel` only runs when a prefill batch holds two or more sequences (a single sequence goes to Triton), so it shows up under concurrency. Triton on the same inputs matches an fp32 reference. Since #43246, main defaults K3 prefill on Blackwell to FlashInfer, so this affects setups that select `nvidia_kda` explicitly.

| prefill batch (random token ids, Kimi-K3, 8 x B300) | broken answers, `nvidia_kda` | broken answers, `triton` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 x 8,192 | 18 / 20 | 0 / 20 |
| 4 x 4,096 | 35 / 40 | 0 / 40 |
| 8 x 2,048 | 78 / 80 | 0 / 80 |
| 8 x 1,024 | 1 / 80 | 1 / 80 |

It is not the FP8 KV cache or the bf16 SSM state (`--mamba-ssm-dtype float32` fails the same way), and it reproduces on the stock image with no local patches. One observation, not a diagnosis: in the failing head, a channel's cumulative log-decay inside a 64-token chunk falls below -88.7 (the fp32 `exp` underflow point) by token 35.

### Reproduction

Kernel level, one GPU, about 10 s, no model needed ([files](https://github.com/Venkat2811/sglang/tree/repro/k3-nvidia-kda-nan/k3_nvidia_kda_nan)):

```
python3 repro_nvidia_kda_nan.py minimal.pt
```

`minimal.pt` is one KDA head (model layer 5, TP rank 7), 2,048 tokens, with the inputs exactly as passed to `NvidiaKDAKernel.extend`. The vendored pipeline gives NaN from token 1,792; Triton `chunk_kda` and an fp32 token-by-token reference agree to 1.4e-4.

<details><summary>Server level (8 x B300, Kimi-K3)</summary>

```
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.89 \
  --context-length 1048576 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --prefill-attention-backend trtllm_mla --linear-attn-prefill-backend nvidia_kda --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --page-size 64
```

After `/flush_cache`, send 8 concurrent `/generate` requests of 2,048 random token ids each (`max_new_tokens` 8, `return_logprob` true). Most answers have NaN logprobs. With `--linear-attn-prefill-backend triton`, none do.
</details>
